newsitem.title: GERMANY: Minister wants cull of British cattle in Germany.
newsitem.headline: Minister wants cull of British cattle in Germany.

text.p: BONN, Jan 22 - German Farm Minister Jochen Borchert said on Wednesday he supported a mass slaughter of cattle originating from Britain, a day after officials confirmed the first case of a cow born in Germany with mad cow disease.
Borchert told ARD German television there were about 3,000 cattle in Germany that had been imported from Britain and that they had produced about 7,000 calves.
He proposed a cull of all those animals and said the carcasses should be incinerated "so that there are no risks in future and consumers will not lose confidence again".

"We were prepared for such cases," Borchert said, adding that the case of bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE) or madcow disease confirmed on Tuesday did not pose any risks to the public because the animal had been under surveillance.
Germany has confirmed the first case of a cow born in the country to die of mad cow disease and called on the European Union to act soon to prevent similar cases.
The Agriculture Ministry confirmed that tests on the brain of the Galloway cow had shown signs of BSE. The cow was born in Germany in 1992, the calf of a cow imported from Britain.
Germany has had four previous cases of BSE, all in cattle imported from Britain where the disease is most widespread with 165,000 cases in the past 10 years.
The possibility that the cow was infected by contaminated feed had been ruled out, the ministry said, leaving only the possibility that it had been infected by its mother.
